institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: High academic standards, good university, nature experiences, courses in english.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was a truly great experience to study abroad, especially because I was so lucky to get to study with and meet people from all over the world and though it sounds like a cliché it really broadened my horizon.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy, the university information side, was very simillar to the danish - so it was easy to find information and you also received many emails with the relevant information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didnt receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was satisfied.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy, I applied through Samskipnad, and got a housing offer I agreed to accept.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived very close to the university, in Dramsvegen, Panorama and that was a very nice place. Very newly renovated and everything worked smoothly. Great view.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think they made a lot effort in Tromsø to accomondate all students with housing, and I think the condiditon of the different housings seems fair.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I just did it online. It was easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just registrated online and all the information about the process you got through a mail.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: different numbers you could call and mail you could write to.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very, I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just do it in good time and everything will be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the academic programme, although it was a bit different from the University in Copenhagen, the level of the academic readings was high. The lectors had a somewhat different teaching style sometimes, but I still got a lot out of the classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was sutiable for MA courses. The readings was at a high level although the way of approaching the academic litterature was somewhat different and sometimes it was more repetative than analytic. But the professors are all very well educated and informed, so if you want to learn - you will.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think the style of teaching at my host university was sometimes more repetative and covered a great deal of knowledge which meant that sometimes you didnt get the chance of really focusing on one case or subject at the time and really imerse your self in the material, because you had to get through so much. But I do think the teachers was at the same academic level as UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Integrated Peace and Conflict studies 
Conflict, culture and society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend both, but I would foremost recommend ; Integrated peace and conflict studies, because it strech over a longer time, almost 2 months- thereby creating more space and time for learning. besides that, the course was a really  great opportunity of improving my english because all the classes, readings and exams was in english. The teachers and the students in this course came from all over the world and that made the learning outcome very multiple and unique. I will highly recommend this course if one is interested in, Political theory, Sociology, Anthropology,history and politics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy winter close and shoes, because I didnt bring enough. But you can bye so much equipment in Tromsø for all sort of winter and outdoor activities very cheap, so I actually think I saved money compared to if I bought it in Denmark. But it is good to rememeber when one lays a budget, to take these costs into account.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Winter closing, spikes, outdoor gear was much cheaper than I expected. Food was a bit expensive, but not as bad as I thought. If you just try to eat sensible you can spend more or less on food as you would in Denmark ( especially if you come from copenhagen, the price level is pretty similar).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really think that the non academic opportunities, was very good. There were so many things going on all the times and samskipnad was very good to make arrangements of differents hiking trips, sauna, movie nights and so on. I will recommend though that you join a lot of different facebook pages, because that makes it easier.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts. There was a lot of athletic or sports activities because Tromsø is surrounded by beautiful nature, mountations, waters etc. Hiking trips, weekend tours, bowling, artcrafts, knitting nights, waffle fridays, and many more

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would defiantly recommend the outdoor tours, because if you dont have a car is it not so easy to come to some of the more unique nature spots and you also get to meet people in a different way when you are out hiking for a whole day and sitting by the fire together. But also the knitting nights and yoga was very nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips in the nature! Tromsø  and the surroundings areas are the most beautiful places in the world. You can get some nature experiences you wouldnt dream off, and I am so greatful for these experiences. Go out in the nature and dont stay indoor, that is my biggest advice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, norway is very similar to denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The northern norwegians are a bit closed and can seem very introvert, so my advice is to join in on a lot of activites and talk to other international students, because there are so many and people are more open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did find the northern norwegians way of being a bit challenging,, they were difficult to talk to and people seemed very introverts. The darkness was also and experience.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate the nature and Tromsø is also a beautiful city with a lot of cultural experiences.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring warm closing and good hiking shoes. experience and most of all - enjoy the nature. Go on trips, do things with other people- challenge your self.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would say that you do spend a lot of money because Norway is expensive, so if you have to opportunity apply for some fundings and scholarships, because that really helped me a lot. And also dont bring to much stuff, you can buy all you need up in Tromsø.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new friends I have met from all over the world, the beautiful hikes and nature and the other perspectives I have gotten on life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Defiantly the darkness when in came, it was very dark and also the norwegian people are not very outgoing, so I definatly recommend to try to make friends from other countries.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
